title: Rafael and the Extraction
premise: Yara Almeida, a whistle-blower living under four names after exposing a private intelligence consortium, receives a voiceprint message that unlocks a dead server in Lisbon — a server only their original self could open. The message comes from Marta Vidal, the consortium's former chief analyst, who wants to defect and carries proof that Yara's exposure was orchestrated to flush out other leakers. Yara is recruited by a fractured extraction network to bring Marta out of Portugal, but every step of the route feels pre-scripted, and Yara begins to suspect Marta is bait for a larger trap. In the climax, Yara turns the trap inside out by feeding the consortium a fabricated version of themselves, forcing the hunters to reveal their hand; Marta is real, but her defection was half-coerced, and she chooses Yara's side at the border. The novel ends with Yara surrendering their four names and publishing everything under one true identity — survival purchased at the price of invisibility, and freedom purchased at the price of safety.
about_author: Tamsin Montrose is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent a decade writing risk assessments for NGOs operating in hostile jurisdictions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose competence is their only armor, from a coastal town she declines to name.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A routine morning in Rotterdam under the name 'Ines Duarte': cash jobs, burner rotations, the ritual of checking three dead-drops that never contain anything. The chapter establishes the rules that keep Yara alive and the loneliness beneath them. Emotional beat: disciplined calm masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. An encrypted voicemail plays a voiceprint phrase Yara hasn't spoken in five years — their original name. It unlocks a dormant server in Lisbon containing a single file: a flight manifest and the words 'Marta Vidal wants out.' Emotional beat: vertigo; the past has found a door.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with flashbacks to the leak five years ago and the consortium's retaliation that killed their colleague Tomás. We learn why four names exist and why contact means death. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into caution.

chapters.title: The Network of Strangers
chapters.summary: Yara contacts the fractured extraction cell through a classified ad cipher. Introduces Odile, the paranoid coordinator in Marseille, and Brecht, a smuggler who owes Yara a debt. They agree to assess the Lisbon request — reluctantly. Emotional beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Lisbon, Under an Old Sky
chapters.summary: Yara arrives in Portugal as 'Rui Costa,' walking streets they once called home. Surveillance tradecraft intercut with memory: the café where they first copied the files. Someone is following them — or are they imagining it? Emotional beat: homesickness as danger.

chapters.title: Marta Vidal
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Inside the consortium's Lisbon office, she copies a drive while attending her own farewell party. She knows she's being watched and does it anyway. Her chapters reveal the consortium's internal rot and her own complicity. Emotional beat: terror braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Handoff That Felt Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. First contact with Marta in a tram tunnel; she passes a sample of the evidence — shipping records tying the consortium to assassinations dressed as accidents. It's exactly what Yara hoped for, which is exactly what worries them. Emotional beat: hope curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Odile's Doubt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, via secure call. She runs counter-analysis on the manifest and finds the extraction route too clean — checkpoints absent where the consortium always posts them. She suspects a scripted corridor. Yara insists on proceeding. Emotional beat: friction between caution and momentum.

chapters.title: Brecht's Boat
chapters.summary: Brecht's POV. He preps a fishing trawler in Setúbal for a run to Tangier, complaining about the cargo: two people instead of crates. His pragmatism offers dark comic relief and a ground-level view of the plan's fragility. Emotional beat: gallows humor.

chapters.title: What Marta Carries
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. The full archive: not just crimes but personnel files — including Yara's own, marked 'ASSET UNRESOLVED.' Marta realizes Yara wasn't hunted five years ago; they were cultivated. Emotional beat: dawning horror at what she's carrying toward whom.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Doors
chapters.summary: Introduce Director Kessler, the consortium's counterintelligence chief, in his POV. Elegant, patient, he explains to a subordinate why leaving one exit open catches more rats than sealing them all. He approves 'Phase Corridor.' Emotional beat: cold intellectual menace.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Dry-run of the route: safehouse, tram, dock, boat. Everything works on the first try. Yara, who trusts nothing that works, starts building a second route no one else knows. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into craft.

chapters.title: The Tail Who Wanted to Be Seen
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara spots surveillance and lets it see them deliberately, feeding a false pattern. But the tail's behavior suggests they wanted to be spotted — a message, or a test. Emotional beat: the hunter's game inverted.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. In a safehouse, she tells Yara a partial truth: she helped design the system that destroyed them. Yara already knows. The scene is a duel of omissions, ending in a fragile, unearned trust neither can afford. Emotional beat: intimacy built on mutual leverage.

chapters.title: Kessler's Album
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. He reviews photos of Yara across five years and four names, revealing how long the consortium has watched. He speaks aloud to the photo: 'You were the best thing we ever made.' Emotional beat: violation without touch.

chapters.title: The Server Speaks Back
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Digging into the unlocked Lisbon server, Yara finds its access log: it was opened remotely twice before — once by Kessler. The voiceprint invitation may have been his, not Marta's. Emotional beat: the floor gives way.

chapters.title: Split the Difference
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The cell fractures: Odile wants abort, Brecht wants payment, Yara proposes a split operation — a decoy extraction along the obvious route, the real one hidden. Odile agrees only if she controls the decoy. Emotional beat: reluctant consensus.

chapters.title: The Decoy Departs
chapters.summary: Brecht's POV. The trawler leaves Setúbal with two hired stand-ins dressed for night passage. Brecht hates using strangers as props but takes the money. We feel the moral cost of tradecraft. Emotional beat: guilt at sea.

chapters.title: Interdiction
chapters.summary: Consortium operatives' POV (a field team led by a woman called Sable). They intercept the trawler off Cascais and find no Marta, no Yara — only paid actors. Kessler, watching remotely, smiles: the real route is now narrowed to three options. Emotional beat: professional admiration turning predatory.

chapters.title: The Road North
chapters.summary: Yara and Marta's alternating POV. The real route goes overland: Porto, then the Spanish border by freight train. Confined together, they trade life stories; Marta's daughter, estranged, becomes the human stake. Emotional beat: tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A former asset herself, she recognizes Yara's tradecraft signature — she was trained alongside them years ago, before either knew the consortium's face. She requests the lead on the overland intercept. Emotional beat: recognition as wound.

chapters.title: Freight and Silence
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Hiding among machinery parts in a slow train through Galicia, Yara realizes the manifest numbers on the crates match the assassination shipments in Marta's archive — they're riding inside the evidence. Emotional beat: grim irony, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: The Border That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. At the crossing, guards wave them through without checking papers — the absence of friction Odile predicted. Marta understands they're being herded toward something worse than capture: a staged public 'rescue' that will discredit the archive. Emotional beat: dread of the gilded cage.

chapters.title: Odile's Sacrifice
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Running the decoy network in Marseille, she detects the consortium tracing her relay chain. Instead of fleeing, she floods the channel with garbage data to buy Yara hours, knowing it burns her location. Emotional beat: quiet heroism, farewell without goodbye.

chapters.title: What Odile Left
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A final packet from Odile arrives posthumously: Kessler's Phase Corridor blueprint, plus a note — 'You were never the target. The archive was. Make it loud enough they can't bury it.' Emotional beat: grief converted to mandate.

chapters.title: The Trap Has a Shape
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Assembling everything, Yara maps the trap: a safehouse in Bilbao where 'extraction' would be staged on camera, the archive seized, Marta discredited as unstable, Yara framed as a consortium double agent. Every piece fits. Emotional beat: clarity as cold comfort.

chapters.title: Turning the Key
chapters.summary: Yara and Marta plot the inversion: let the trap close, but replace its contents. Marta will carry a doctored archive; the real one goes out via a dead-drop mesh Odile built. Yara will play the role Kessler wrote for them — convincingly. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into audacity.

chapters.title: Brecht Comes Back
chapters.summary: Brecht's POV. Having survived the decoy fiasco, he volunteers for the exfil leg, refusing payment this time. His arc completes from mercenary to accomplice. He brings a detail that saves them later: the harbor master in Bilbao owes him. Emotional beat: unexpected loyalty.

chapters.title: The Performance Begins
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara walks into the Bilbao safehouse visibly frightened, playing the cornered whistle-blower Kessler scripted. Sable watches from cover, and something in Yara's performance rings false to her trained eye. Emotional beat: high-wire tension.

chapters.title: Kessler's Victory Lap
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. He confronts 'captured' Yara, monologuing just enough to confirm the frame-up on tape — which is, unknown to him, Yara recording his admissions against the consortium's own encrypted channel. Emotional beat: arrogance as fatal flaw.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Reviewing the footage, she spots the second camera angle — Yara's. Realizing Kessler has been played and that she was always disposable, she makes a decision: she doesn't raise the alarm when Marta slips the net. Emotional beat: defection in miniature.

chapters.title: The Archive Goes Loud
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, rapid cuts. Odile's mesh detonates: the real archive publishes simultaneously to forty outlets. Newsrooms light up across Europe. Kessler's channel floods with his own recorded voice confessing. Emotional beat: catharsis at scale.

chapters.title: Chasing the Ghost of Yourself
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Escape through Bilbao's port as the consortium's command structure implodes and orders become contradictory. Sable, now openly turned, covers their flank against her own former team. Emotional beat: running no longer feels like losing.

chapters.title: Kessler Unbound
chapters.summary: Kessler's POV. Denounced by his own board as a liability, he goes rogue, deciding that if the consortium falls, it falls on his terms — he'll take Marta alive and burn the rest. Emotional beat: power curdling into desperation.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry
chapters.summary: Yara, Marta, and Brecht race for Santander as Kessler closes in. Marta hesitates at the gangway — her daughter is in Portugal, and leaving means exile forever. Yara tells her the truth about their own lost family. Emotional beat: the price named aloud.

chapters.title: Pier Fight
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Kessler corners them on the pier; Sable intervenes, and in the struggle Kessler is arrested by arriving Spanish police tipped off anonymously — by Yara, using the last of Odile's channels. Emotional beat: violence brief, consequences lasting.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Marta's POV. Weeks later, she testifies before a parliamentary inquiry, the archive authenticated. She names names, including her own. Her daughter watches from the gallery. Emotional beat: accountability as redemption, imperfect but real.

chapters.title: One Name
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara retires the four aliases, publishes a first-person account under their birth name, and accepts the exposure they spent five years fleeing. Threats arrive within hours — and so do letters from other whistle-blowers. Emotional beat: terror and liberation indistinguishable.

chapters.title: The Extraction
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Yara's POV. Months on: Yara, Sable, and Brecht quietly run a small network extracting others like Marta. The last scene mirrors the first — a morning routine, a checked dead-drop — except this time the drop contains a plea for help, and Yara answers it. Emotional beat: survival repurposed as purpose.
